source: AI Video Bootcamp - AI Advertisement Workflow Checklist, Social Media AD Structure, and the five-step UGC method
note: The ad material as data. Beat timing is capped, not proportional: the checklist demands the product appear within 5-10 seconds, and ANY percentage split breaks that as the ad gets longer. An even split puts beat 4 at 18s in a 30s ad; even a front-loaded 52% split puts it at 31s in a 60s ad. So the setup (beats 1-3) is capped in absolute seconds and beat 4 absorbs the remaining time. See `timing`.

timing.note: setup = min(setup_share * total, setup_cap). close = min(close_share * total, close_cap). Beat 4 takes what is left, because the product demonstration is the part that should grow when an ad gets longer - the hook and the CTA do not.

tiktok.label: TikTok / Reels
tiktok.tone: vertical, phone-shot, deliberately unpolished - native beats polished here
tiktok.note: Hook first. If the first clip runs past 3 seconds people scroll before the cut.

youtube.label: YouTube
youtube.tone: longer, value-driven, storytelling - you have room to earn attention
youtube.note: The only platform where the story can breathe. Still show the product by 10s.

instagram.label: Instagram
instagram.tone: aesthetic, polished, brand-heavy - the opposite of the TikTok cut
instagram.note: Looks matter more than rawness here. Same ad, different grade.

meta-google.label: Meta / Google Ads
meta-google.cta_style: explicit, clickable, stated once and clearly
meta-google.tone: transactional, clickable, concise - this is a click, not a vibe
meta-google.note: Shortest and most direct. The CTA is the point, not a garnish.

beats.label: Call out the pain
beats.role: Name the problem so precisely that the right person stops scrolling.
beats.must_do: Say the specific, embarrassing, daily version of the problem - not the category.
examples: Your hair gets greasy 5 hours after washing it.
You're shedding more hair in the shower than your dog.
You bought a £20 shampoo and it made it worse.
beats.note: This is where A/B variants come from - write three, test three.

beats.label: Make it relatable
beats.role: Show you know what they have already tried and why it failed.
beats.must_do: List the failed attempts by name. Recognition is what earns the next five seconds.
examples: You've tried everything - drugstore brands, salon brands, TikTok hacks - and still your scalp's a mess and your ends feel like straw.

beats.label: Offer a shift
beats.role: Turn the problem around. Either declare the change, or ask what if.
beats.must_do: Pivot from what is wrong to what could be different - without naming the product yet.
examples: That's why we made a shampoo that actually works with your hair - not against it.
What if you could go 3 days without washing your hair - and still feel fresh?

beats.label: Introduce the product solution
beats.role: Name the product and say what it actually is.
beats.must_do: Name it, then say the mechanism plainly. This beat MUST start inside 5-10 seconds.
examples: It's called LumaWash. A shampoo made with zero sulfates, zero harsh chemicals - and a formula that balances your scalp naturally.
beats.note: The one beat where specification language is correct. 'Sell the feeling' governs beats 1-3; by here the ad has earned the right to say what the thing does.

beats.label: Stack social proof and urgency
beats.role: Prove other people bought it, then give a reason to act now.
beats.must_do: BOTH halves. Proof without urgency is the common failure, and it looks finished.
examples: Customers say their hair changed in just 3 washes.
And this week only, we're giving 20% off to first-time customers.

emotions.note: Step 4 - forget the product. People do not buy a formula, they buy how they expect to feel. Beats 1-3 are written in this vocabulary.

confidence.label: Confidence
confidence.feeling: being seen the way you want to be seen
confidence.say: you walk in and you are not worrying about it

belonging.label: Belonging
belonging.say: everyone you know has this problem and nobody says it

frustration.label: Frustration
frustration.say: you already wasted money on three of these

aspiration.label: Aspiration
aspiration.feeling: the version of your life that works

fear-of-missing-out.label: Fear of missing out
fear-of-missing-out.say: your friend already switched and did not tell you

items.text: The objective is stated (awareness, traffic, conversions)
The target audience is written down: age, pain points, desires, niche
The platform is chosen
The ad length is set and inside the platform's range
The CTA type is decided
It grabs attention instantly
It is visually disruptive or emotionally engaging
The hook lands inside the platform's hook window
The first clip is under 3 seconds
A clear, short script exists
Each scene is planned visually - camera angle and framing
It follows a proven arc (problem to agitation to solution)
The product or offer is shown within 5-10 seconds
Image generation tool chosen
Video generation tool chosen
Lipsync / voice tool chosen
Editing tool chosen
Script writing tool chosen
Outputs match the brand tone and style
Subtitles added if needed
It matches what the client asked for
Cinematic or native for the platform, deliberately
The stills are scroll-stopping and real-looking
Consistent lighting and camera motion across shots
The advert targets an emotion
You know how the viewer is left feeling
Correct aspect ratio
Platform-native pacing
Thumbnail / opening frame chosen for stopping power
CTA clearly visible or spoken
Previewed on mobile before publishing
A/B versions ready with different hooks
Feedback asked from peers or a test audience
Best performer saved for future reference

publishing.note: Reference only - the app does not act on any of this, in the way the film glossary defines terms without using them. Platform craft, not tooling.

items.text: Upload 1080p at 30fps. 4K at 60fps gets downscaled by TikTok and looks worse, not better.
9:16 for TikTok and Reels, 16:9 for YouTube and TV, 4:5 for feed posts.
Keep the opening shot under 3 seconds. A slow first cut is where viewers leave.
Add text. If people are reading, they are still watching - it buys watch time.
Four at most. More than that and the algorithm gets a confused signal about the topic.
Three to five posts a day is the ceiling, and leave 1-2 hours between them.
Post at the same time daily, so metrics reflect the video rather than the hour.
Watch time is the one that matters. If viewers drop at 2 seconds, the hook is the problem, not the offer.
If one video is working, post the next one while it is still moving. Do not wait days.
Private a video rather than deleting it.
The video is the hard part. Once it exists, posting it to every platform costs minutes.
Keep every post inside one niche so the platform knows who to show it to.
